title: Kernel and injectivity of a fixed tensor test at contracted primes
statement:
Let $\varphi:R\to A$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, let $u:M\to M'$ be an $A$-linear map, and fix an $R$-module $N$. Use localizations [def-weil-pbc-module-localization], spectra [def-weil-affine-spectrum], and tensor products [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Put $T_N=u\otimes_R1_N:M\otimes_RN\to M'\otimes_RN$, with the $A$-actions on the first tensor factors, and let $K=\{z\in M\otimes_RN:T_N(z)=0\}$, an $A$-submodule. For each prime $\mathfrak q$ of $A$ put $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$ and $T_{\mathfrak q,N}=u_{\mathfrak q}\otimes_{R_{\mathfrak p}}1_{N_{\mathfrak p}}$, using the canonical $R_{\mathfrak p}$-actions on $M_{\mathfrak q}$ and $M'_{\mathfrak q}$. The map induced by localizing the inclusion $K\hookrightarrow M\otimes_RN$ and then applying $c_{M,N}$ of [lem-trf-contracted-prime-tensor-comparison] is an $A_{\mathfrak q}$-linear isomorphism
$$K_{\mathfrak q}\xrightarrow{\sim}\ker(T_{\mathfrak q,N}).$$
Moreover, $T_N$ is injective if and only if $T_{\mathfrak q,N}$ is injective for every prime $\mathfrak q$ of $A$, and also if and only if $T_{\mathfrak m,N}$ is injective for every maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$ of $A$. No flatness, finite-generation, or finite-presentation assumption is imposed.

source.place: Tag 05CL, lemma-universally-injective-check-stalks, proof: the localized kernel argument for (5) implies (1), and exact localization for (1) implies (4), with a fixed test module

proof.text: Put $X=M\otimes_RN$, $Y=M'\otimes_RN$, $T=T_N$, and let $i:K\hookrightarrow X$ be the inclusion. Since $T$ is $A$-linear, $K$ is an $A$-submodule and $K\xrightarrow{i}X\xrightarrow{T}Y$ is exact. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact] over $A$ at $A\setminus\mathfrak q$. The image of $i_{\mathfrak q}$ is $\ker T_{\mathfrak q}$. It is injective: if $k/s$ maps to zero, the fraction criterion gives $t\notin\mathfrak q$ with $ti(k)=0$, hence $tk=0$ and $k/s=0$. Thus $i_{\mathfrak q}$ identifies $K_{\mathfrak q}$ with $\ker T_{\mathfrak q}$.

By [lem-trf-contracted-prime-tensor-comparison], $c_{M',N}T_{\mathfrak q}=T_{\mathfrak q,N}c_{M,N}$ and both $c$ maps are $A_{\mathfrak q}$-linear isomorphisms. Consequently $c_{M,N}$ restricts to an isomorphism of kernels: $T_{\mathfrak q}x=0$ implies $T_{\mathfrak q,N}c_{M,N}x=0$; conversely, if $T_{\mathfrak q,N}y=0$, set $x=c_{M,N}^{-1}y$, so $c_{M',N}T_{\mathfrak q}x=0$ and $T_{\mathfrak q}x=0$. Composing with step 1 gives exactly the asserted map from $K_{\mathfrak q}$, including its normalization by the localized inclusion.

source.place: Tag 05CL (lemma-universally-injective-check-stalks), displayed tensor identities and their application to kernels

proof.text: If $T_N$ is injective, $K=0$, hence every $K_{\mathfrak q}=0$ by the fraction construction. The kernel isomorphism in step 2 gives $\ker T_{\mathfrak q,N}=0$, so every $T_{\mathfrak q,N}$ is injective. This includes maximal ideals, which are prime: if $ab\in\mathfrak m$ and $a\notin\mathfrak m$, write $1=r+ca$ with $r\in\mathfrak m$, giving $b=rb+cab\in\mathfrak m$.

source.place: Tag 05CL (lemma-universally-injective-check-stalks), implication (1) to (4) for a fixed test module

proof.text:
Conversely assume $T_{\mathfrak m,N}$ injective for every maximal $\mathfrak m$. Steps 1--2 give $K_{\mathfrak m}=0$. If $0
e k\in K$, its annihilator $I=\{a\in A:ak=0\}$ is an ideal and is proper since $1k=k
e0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal] choose a maximal $\mathfrak m\supseteq I$. Since $k/1=0$ in $K_{\mathfrak m}$, [def-weil-pbc-module-localization] supplies $s
otin\mathfrak m$ with $sk=0$, contradicting $s\in I\subseteq\mathfrak m$. Thus $K=0$ and $T_N$ is injective. The all-prime hypothesis implies the all-maximal one by step 3, completing both equivalences.
